area: renderer boot to first interactive frame (index.html -> index chunk -> boot chunk -> App -> WorkspaceRoot -> viewer -> explorer usable -> Cmd+P usable)
timeline:
Measured live over CDP against the installed build (~/Applications/Horus.app, app.asar built 12:32:28, same timestamp as out/renderer). Two real sessions probed, ports 9490 and 9491. I did not restart the user's app; all numbers are warm.

t=0 navigation start (src/renderer/index.html, file:// inside app.asar). responseEnd 45.5 ms, domInteractive 89.1 ms, DOMContentLoaded 93.3 ms, load 95.9 ms.
t=46-90 ms  index.html head: CSP meta (electron.vite.config.ts:17-45), 5-rule inline critical style (index.html:8-16), then <script type=module src=./assets/index-CaNbrFQL.js> plus <link rel=preload as=style boot-B2Joa_jX.css> and <link rel=modulepreload boot-B2rRKoKF.js> injected by preloadBootChunkPlugin (electron.vite.config.ts:136-163). Only <div class="boot-drag"> (index.html:20) is on screen.
t=87.6-92.8 ms  horus:renderer-loaded (main.tsx:4 -> startupMetrics.ts:13). main.tsx is 9 lines: stamp restore hint on <html>, fire getSessionSnapshot(), dynamic import('./boot').
t=100-112 ms  first-paint (dark ground, no content).
t=93-142 ms  index-CaNbrFQL.js's __vitePreload shim creates <link rel=stylesheet boot-B2Joa_jX.css> (171,776 B, 1,266 rules) and AWAITS its load before importing boot-B2rRKoKF.js (439,332 B). boot.tsx:14-15 fires the two fontsource CSS imports (not awaited); boot.tsx:17 loadPreferences() reads localStorage; boot.tsx:18 initialWorkspacePaint(window.repository.cachedWorkspace) — already parsed in the preload via ipcRenderer.sendSync (src/preload/index.ts:55).
t=142-233 ms  ONE 91 ms long task (PerformanceObserver longtask buffered:true -> {name:"self", start:142, duration:91}). This is boot.tsx:20-30 `await Promise.all([preloadWorkspaceRoot(), preloadWorkspaceViewer(...)])` resolving and every module body executing back to back — WorkspaceRoot 268,669 B, copyFilePath 301,887 B, ViewerProviders 10,796 B, useReviewLoadState 12,513 B, pierre-dark 30,549 B, BackToTopButton 611,171 B, MultiFileReview 103,345 B — then createRoot().render() (boot.tsx:32-38) and React's first render+commit.
t=162.8-171.4 ms  horus:explorer-committed (RepositoryWorkspace.tsx:1297) and horus:viewer-committed (MultiFileReview.tsx:1065 / DiffSurface.tsx:535) — child layout effects.
t=177.9-197.2 ms  horus:react-committed (App.tsx:636) — the parent layout effect runs last.
t=284 ms  first-contentful-paint. The window is blank from 112 ms to 284 ms.
t=4541.7 ms (port-9490 session)  horus:snapshot-ready (App.tsx:698) — main finally delivers the restored snapshot; this is the lead's confirmed 3.8 s `git ls-files --others --ignored`. In the port-9491 session the mark never fired within 100 s, because applySnapshot early-returns on snapshotLooksUnchanged (App.tsx:696-697) before marking.

Steady state: 218 light-DOM nodes, 1,291 including shadow roots, 26 rendered tree rows (@pierre/trees virtualizes — nothing renders 20k rows), 14-16 MB JS heap, 4 stylesheets, 14 font faces all font-display:swap with only the two latin subsets loaded, full style recalc 0.2 ms.

Cmd+P: the palette chunk is 10,060 B and is warmed twice — requestIdleCallback once a snapshot exists (App.tsx:977-982) and on the first Meta keydown (App.tsx:219), so opening is instant. The cost is typing: useRepositorySearch lives inside AppLayout (App.tsx:552) and workspaceContentSearch (App.tsx:555-558) is rebuilt per keystroke in single-file view, breaking the memo on AgentSessionLayout and re-rendering WorkspaceRoot -> RepositoryWorkspace -> Explorer on every character.

Verdict for this area: the renderer's own boot is ~200 ms warm and is NOT the 3.8 s startup problem (that is the main-process git walk the lead confirmed). What the renderer does contribute is a single 91 ms main-thread block landing exactly when the window appears, 1.87 MB of JS+CSS that must fully execute before React mounts at all, and a per-keystroke full-workspace re-render behind Cmd+P.

findings.title: boot.tsx awaits the whole viewer chunk graph (~1.87 MB) before createRoot().render() — regression introduced by e18053e
findings.mechanism: When a cached workspace exists (the normal restore path, and the path a Raycast horus:// open also lands on) mountApp blocks on Promise.all([preloadWorkspaceRoot(), preloadWorkspaceViewer(cachedPaint.workspaceView)]) before React mounts anything. That resolves only after WorkspaceRoot-DzrbT5iL.js (268,669 B) plus its static deps copyFilePath-C07D3-Xy.js (301,887 B), ViewerProviders (10,796 B), useReviewLoadState (12,513 B), pierre-dark (30,549 B), plus the viewer branch BackToTopButton-C2hfwQQH.js (611,171 B) and MultiFileReview-B7hs9zS1.js (103,345 B) have all been read from the asar, parsed and executed. Nothing is on screen but the 40px drag strip for that whole time. React already has both fallbacks for this: App.tsx:340-357 CachedWorkspaceFallback renders the cached sidebar when getLoadedWorkspaceRoot() is null, and WorkspaceSkeleton.tsx:41-52 WorkspaceCodeSkeleton covers the viewer slot.
findings.evidence: `git show e18053e -- src/renderer/src/boot.tsx` shows the file was created in that commit with the blocking await; the code it replaced in main.tsx was fire-and-forget — `void preloadWorkspaceRoot().catch(...)` under the comment "Start the matching UI chunks in parallel, but do not await them". Live marks: horus:renderer-loaded 92.8 ms, single longtask start 142 dur 91, horus:react-committed 197.2 ms, first-paint 112 ms, first-contentful-paint 284 ms. Chunk graph from the built output: WorkspaceRoot-DzrbT5iL.js statically imports copyFilePath-C07D3-Xy.js, ViewerProviders-CwKApq7y.js, useReviewLoadState-nxeBxob_.js, pierre-dark-CyvmCCZW.js; MultiFileReview-B7hs9zS1.js statically imports BackToTopButton-C2hfwQQH.js.
findings.fix: Delete the await. Replace boot.tsx:20-30 with unconditional fire-and-forget preloads: `void preloadWorkspaceRoot().catch(() => undefined)` and, when cachedPaint.snapshot != null, `void preloadWorkspaceViewer(cachedPaint.workspaceView).catch(() => undefined)`; keep the existing sessionSnapshot.then branch for the no-cache case. Move createRoot().render() to run immediately after loadPreferences(). App already renders CachedWorkspaceFallback (App.tsx:487-493) while WorkspaceRoot is null and re-renders through useSyncExternalStore(subscribeWorkspaceRoot) (App.tsx:665-669) the moment the chunk lands, so nothing downstream needs to change. If the await was added to suppress a fallback flash, gate the fallback on a 60 ms timer instead of on chunk load.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 90-140 ms warm to first contentful frame; substantially more on the first launch after an update when the V8 code cache is cold

findings.title: BackToTopButton-C2hfwQQH.js is a 611 KB shared viewer chunk: 257 KB @pierre/diffs + 146 KB parse5 + ~90 KB micromark/mdast/hast, all on the pre-mount path
findings.mechanism: Rollup put every module shared by DiffSurface and MultiFileReview into one chunk and named it after the smallest module in it (BackToTopButton.tsx, 699 bytes) — that is why the chunk name says nothing about the 611 KB inside; copyFilePath-C07D3-Xy.js is named the same accidental way. parse5 is present only because rehype-raw needs a real HTML parser, and the whole markdown pipeline is dragged in statically by ReviewComments/GitHubMarkdownContent, which both viewers import eagerly even though a review usually has zero comments.
findings.evidence: Byte attribution decoded from BackToTopButton-C2hfwQQH.js.map: @pierre/diffs 256,834 (FileDiff 41,023, style.js 37,856, InteractionManager 31,320, DiffHunksRenderer 26,076, VirtualizedFileDiff 25,549, File 23,120, VirtualizedFile 12,836, FileRenderer 11,260), parse5 146,415 (parser/index 46,732, tokenizer/index 45,835), micromark-core-commonmark 27,520, mdast-util-to-markdown 11,692, mdast-util-to-hast 10,895, mdast-util-from-markdown 10,371, micromark 9,555, hast-util-to-jsx-runtime 5,943, hast-util-raw 5,622, hast-util-sanitize 5,134, unified 4,160, entities 15,495, app 35,032 (ReviewComments.tsx 7,072, dragSelection.ts 5,905, splitDiffResize.ts 5,723).
findings.fix: In src/renderer/src/ReviewComments.tsx replace the static import of GitHubMarkdownContent with `const GitHubMarkdownContent = lazy(() => import('./GitHubMarkdownContent'))` and wrap its uses in `{body}}>`. That moves react-markdown + rehype-raw + rehype-sanitize + remark-gfm + parse5 + micromark + the mdast/hast stack (~240 KB) out of the shared viewer chunk into a chunk fetched only when a comment thread actually renders. Verify afterwards that the shared chunk drops to ~370 KB and that parse5 no longer appears in its source map.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 25-45 ms warm (parse plus top-level execution of ~240 KB); removes 240 KB from every cold start

findings.title: The whole shiki/textmate/oniguruma tokenizer stack (302 KB chunk) is loaded and executed on the MAIN thread at startup, duplicating the highlighter worker
findings.mechanism: Highlighting itself runs in worker-JZSb44JN.js (207,560 B), which loads its own copy of the grammar machinery — so roughly 140 KB of tokenizer code is parsed and its module bodies executed on the main thread inside the 91 ms boot long task for nothing. The build already proves this class of trim works: dropShikiWasmPlugin (electron.vite.config.ts:165-181) stubs shiki/wasm and saved a 622 KB inlined wasm chunk, and trimShikiThemesPlugin (electron.vite.config.ts:66-134) rewrites shiki/dist/themes.mjs.
findings.evidence: Byte attribution of copyFilePath-C07D3-Xy.js.map: @shikijs/vscode-textmate 42,538, shiki langs-bundle-full 28,709, oniguruma-to-es 26,658, oniguruma-parser 23,987, @shikijs/core 18,141, property-information 17,936, @shikijs/primitive 13,524, @shikijs/engine-oniguruma 7,005, hast-util-to-html 7,989, @pierre/diffs WorkerPoolManager 20,340 + parsePatchFiles 9,541 + iterateOverDiff 9,382. `grep -c 'createHighlighterCore\|createOnigurumaEngine\|createJavaScriptRegexEngine' copyFilePath-C07D3-Xy.js` = 3. Chunk graph shows WorkspaceRoot-DzrbT5iL.js and ViewerProviders-CwKApq7y.js both `from"./copyFilePath-C07D3-Xy.js"`, and WorkspaceRoot is awaited at boot.tsx:22. The 270+ shiki language grammars are dynamic (`import("./typescript-BPQ3VLAy.js")`), so those are correctly lazy.
findings.fix: Add a renderer-only plugin next to dropShikiWasmPlugin that resolves @shikijs/engine-oniguruma, oniguruma-to-es and shiki/dist/langs-bundle-full to throwing stubs, registered in `renderer.plugins` but NOT in `renderer.worker.plugins` (electron.vite.config.ts:231-234 already keeps a separate plugin list for the worker, so the worker keeps the real modules). Before stubbing, put a breakpoint on the three createHighlighter-family call sites to confirm none runs on the main thread. If @pierre/diffs only needs the shiki types there, switch those to `import type`.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 20-40 ms warm; ~140 KB off the pre-mount path

findings.title: @pierre/trees path-store (62 KB) and 30 @pierre/icons (23 KB) sit in the 439 KB boot chunk only because treeExpansion.ts calls prepareFileTreeInput
findings.mechanism: Nothing in the boot chunk renders a tree — the real FileTree lives in WorkspaceRoot-DzrbT5iL.js, which already carries 175,231 bytes of @pierre/trees. The only entry-chunk consumer is workspaceMode.ts:47/48 firstOpenPathForSnapshot -> treeExpansion.ts:21 orderPathsForTree -> prepareFileTreeInput, reached from boot.tsx (via workspaceMode) and App.tsx:642. So the entire SoA path-store is parsed and evaluated at boot to answer the question "which path would the tree show first".
findings.evidence: boot-B2rRKoKF.js byte attribution: react-dom 180,847, app 159,571, @pierre/trees 62,315, @pierre/icons 23,207, react 8,542, scheduler 3,680. The @pierre/trees sources listed in that map are path-store/src/{builder,store,canonical,projection,events,cleanup,soa-node-store,flatten,sort,segments,path,state,child-index,options,internal-types}.js plus preparedInput.js. Measured cost of the call it exists for: prepareFileTreeInput 4.07 ms at the user's real 2,621 paths, 34.87 ms at 20,000 paths.
findings.fix: Replace firstTreePath in treeExpansion.ts with a local folders-first comparator that does not import @pierre/trees — the only property it needs is "directories before files at each level, byte order within a level", a ~15-line sort on split paths. Keep orderPathsForTree (used by RepositoryWorkspace.tsx:381 inside the WorkspaceRoot chunk) importing @pierre/trees. Then confirm the boot chunk source map no longer lists path-store sources. Separately, AppView.tsx:2-24 imports 23 @pierre/icons for Titlebar and Welcome; the Welcome-only ones can move into a lazily imported Welcome.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 10-20 ms warm (parse plus execution of ~85 KB), and it removes the 35 ms tail risk described in RB-05

findings.title: App re-runs initialWorkspacePaint() and firstOpenPathForSnapshot() on every render, and React Compiler compiled zero of App
findings.mechanism: Both are plain call expressions in the component body, not lazy useState initializers, so they run on every render of the root component. initialWorkspacePaint (src/shared/workspaceCache.ts:110-121) calls parseSelectedPath -> paths.includes(raw), a linear scan of up to MAX_CACHED_PATHS = 20,000 (workspaceCache.ts:4). firstOpenPathForSnapshot (workspaceMode.ts:43-49) falls through to firstTreePath(snapshot.paths) -> prepareFileTreeInput over every path whenever the repo is clean or is a plain folder. On top of that, React Compiler bailed on App entirely, so none of its ~40 hooks and derived values are compiler-memoized either.
findings.evidence: Decoding the VLQ mappings of boot-B2rRKoKF.js.map at App.tsx:639 gives the shipped text `const a=om(window.repository?.cachedWorkspace??null),[o,c]=C.useState(a.snapshot),[d,f]=C.useState(a.selectedPath??(a.snapshot==null?null:na(a.snapshot)))` — no memo-cache guard. Scanning 30,000 generated characters from the start of App (minified name Q3) finds zero `qe.c(N)` memo-cache calls, while `grep -oE '[A-Za-z$_]{1,3}\.c\([0-9]+\)' boot-B2rRKoKF.js | wc -l` = 34 for the chunk as a whole (WorkspaceRoot chunk 27, MultiFileReview chunk 17). Bench: prepareFileTreeInput 4.07 ms @2,621 real paths / 34.87 ms @20,000; paths.includes(last) 0.06 ms @20,000.
findings.fix: App.tsx:639 -> `const [cachedPaint] = useState(() => initialWorkspacePaint(window.repository?.cachedWorkspace ?? null))`. App.tsx:641-642 -> `useState(() => cachedPaint.selectedPath ?? (cachedPaint.snapshot == null ? null : firstOpenPathForSnapshot(cachedPaint.snapshot)))`. Separately, find the compiler bailout: rebuild with babel-plugin-react-compiler configured as `{ target: '19', logger: { logEvent: (file, event) => event.kind === 'CompileError' && console.error(file, event) } }` at electron.vite.config.ts:216-220 and fix what App does that the compiler rejects — likeliest are the four useEffectEvent call sites (App.tsx:214, 758, 830, 894) or the mutable folderPickerOpenRef writes inside useCallback bodies (App.tsx:838-857). Getting App compiled is worth more than any single micro-fix here.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 0-35 ms per App render depending on repo size; on a 20k-path folder this is ~35 ms of jank on every root state change

findings.title: Typing in Cmd+P re-renders the entire workspace once per keystroke while the single-file view is active
findings.mechanism: useRepositorySearch owns the query state and lives inside AppLayout, so every keystroke re-renders AppLayout. App.tsx:555-558 then builds `{ query: search.query, results: search.contentResults }` — a fresh object identity per keystroke whenever workspaceView === 'file' — and passes it to AgentSessionLayout, which is memo()'d (App.tsx:355). That one prop breaks the memo, so AgentSessionLayout -> WorkspaceRoot -> RepositoryWorkspace -> Explorer/DiffSurface all re-render on every character. It is compounded by useRepositorySearch.ts:64-96: the effect has `query` in its deps and unconditionally calls setContentResults([]) (a brand-new array every time) plus setSearchingContent(true) plus an IPC window.repository.cancelContentSearch(), outside any transition — so each keystroke costs two extra synchronous renders of that whole subtree on top of the one the input caused. The palette itself is careful (CommandPalette.tsx:340-346 wraps onQueryChange in startTransition, useRepositorySearch.ts:36 uses useDeferredValue) and that care is undone by the effect writing state synchronously afterwards. In multi-file review the memo does hold because workspaceContentSearch is undefined — which matches the user reporting the jank as intermittent.
findings.evidence: App.tsx:555-558 useMemo deps are [search.contentResults, search.query, workspace.workspaceView]; search.contentResults gets a new [] identity from useRepositorySearch.ts:69 and :77 on every keystroke. contentSearch is threaded down RepositoryWorkspace.tsx:1290 -> :1527 -> :946 to DiffSurface.tsx:368-371. Bench proves the ranking is not the culprit: rankFilePaths costs 0.38 ms at the user's 2,621 paths and 1.26-3.05 ms at 20,000 for queries 'a'..'applic'; createFileSearchIndex is memoized on snapshot.paths and costs 0.46 ms / 3.18 ms.
findings.fix: (1) useRepositorySearch.ts:69 and :77 — make the clears identity-stable with a module-level frozen EMPTY_RESULTS: `setContentResults((current) => current.length === 0 ? current : EMPTY_RESULTS)`, and only call setSearchingContent(true) when it is currently false. (2) App.tsx:555-558 — key the memo on `useDeferredValue(search.query)` so the workspace sees at most one update per idle slice. (3) Better still, stop passing content-search state through the workspace tree at all: expose it via a small context that only DiffSurface (DiffSurface.tsx:368) subscribes to, so a keystroke can never re-render Explorer or the tree. (4) Wrap the effect body's state writes in startTransition.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 5-30 ms of main-thread work removed per keystroke — the difference between a dropped frame and none

findings.title: 172 KB / 1,266-rule stylesheet is strictly serial in front of the app JS, and most of it styles lazily loaded surfaces
findings.line: whole file (202,110 bytes source, 171,776 bytes built as boot-B2Joa_jX.css); imported at src/renderer/src/boot.tsx:11
findings.mechanism: boot.tsx:11 imports styles.css into the boot chunk, so Vite emits it as boot-B2Joa_jX.css; the entry shim index-CaNbrFQL.js creates the <link rel=stylesheet> and awaits its load event before it even starts importing boot-B2rRKoKF.js (that is what the __vitePreload wrapper does for .css deps). The rel=preload injected by preloadBootChunkPlugin keeps it warm but does not remove the serialization. Most of the file styles components that are lazy() or dynamically imported and therefore cannot paint for seconds.
findings.evidence: Class-prefix census of styles.css: agent 244 selectors, review 190, performance 155, pr 150, settings 61, markdown 58, git 53, world 50, command 45, welcome 44, terminal 41 — every one of those belongs to TerminalDock, GitHubPanel, SettingsPage, AgentPanel, CommandPalette or PerformanceChart, all of which are lazy. Live CDP probe: the mounted document has 4 stylesheets (inline 5 rules, boot 1,266 rules, inter opsz 7, fira wght 7) and a forced full style recalculation measures 0.20 ms — so this is load/parse cost, not selector-matching cost.
findings.fix: Split styles.css: keep only the tokens (:root and its 163 custom properties), the reset, app-shell, titlebar, workspace/sidebar and explorer rules in the boot stylesheet, and move the agent, performance, pr, settings, terminal, markdown, welcome and command-palette blocks into per-component CSS imported from the lazy components themselves (`import './AgentPanel.css'` inside AgentPanel.tsx) so Vite emits them as sibling chunk CSS. WorkspaceSkeleton.tsx:44 already demonstrates the alternative `<style href precedence>` pattern if separate files are unwanted. Target: boot CSS under 60 KB.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 10-25 ms to first paint (the stylesheet load is serial in front of the boot chunk import)

findings.title: PerformanceHud is mounted unconditionally and fires a main-process IPC metrics sample the instant it mounts, during the startup window
findings.line: 118 (void sample() at mount), 22-23 (2s open / 15s collapsed polling); src/renderer/src/AppView.tsx:36 and :234
findings.mechanism: The HUD is a static import in AppView (AppView.tsx:36) and Titlebar renders it eagerly whenever a snapshot exists (AppView.tsx:231-235). Its mount effect calls `void sample()` immediately (PerformanceHud.tsx:118), which invokes repository.getPerformanceMetrics over IPC; in main that is Electron app.getAppMetrics(), executed on the same main-process thread the lead measured spending 3.8 s in `git ls-files --others --ignored` during restore. It then polls forever at 15 s collapsed / 2 s open and re-samples on every visibilitychange.
findings.evidence: Source-map attribution puts PerformanceHud.tsx at 8,084 bytes inside the 439 KB boot chunk, plus its @pierre/icons IconCiWarningFill import. PerformanceHud.tsx:118 is a bare `void sample()` in the effect body, not gated on idle or on popoverOpen; SAMPLE_INTERVAL_COLLAPSED_MS = 15_000 at line 23.
findings.fix: Make it `const PerformanceHud = lazy(() => import('./PerformanceHud'))` in AppView.tsx and wrap in `<Suspense fallback={null}>` so the 8 KB and the icon leave the boot chunk. Replace PerformanceHud.tsx:118 with `const idle = window.requestIdleCallback(() => void sample())` plus a cancelIdleCallback in the cleanup, and do not sample at all until popoverOpen has been true once — the component already renders an em dash when metrics == null (PerformanceHud.tsx:172).
findings.estimatedGainMs: 3-8 ms of renderer work, plus one IPC round trip and one app.getAppMetrics() call removed from the main process during the startup git walk

findings.title: The startup benchmark probes a selector that a file-view restore can never satisfy, which is why it fails rather than reporting a slow number
findings.line: 107 (review selector), 117-119 (the throw the lead hit), 6 (6 s timeout)
findings.mechanism: All three selectors still exist in the source, so the benchmark is not stale in that sense: #repository-explorer at Explorer.tsx:120, .multi-file-review at MultiFileReview.tsx:882, .multi-file-code-view at retainedWorldCodeView.tsx:215. But .multi-file-code-view only ever renders INSIDE .multi-file-review, so the two-selector list is really one selector, and it only mounts when workspaceView === 'multi'. The user's cached workspace stores workspaceView:'file', so initialWorkspacePaint (workspaceCache.ts:110-121) starts App in file view — and App.applyStartupSnapshot only calls changeWorkspaceView(automaticWorkspaceView(...)) when `appliedSnapshotRef.current?.root !== restoredSnapshot.root` (App.tsx:907-909), which is false because the cached paint already set that ref to the same root. The review surface therefore never mounts and the benchmark throws no matter how fast startup is.
findings.evidence: CDP probe of the running app returned {explorer:true, review:false, diffPanel:true, treeRows:26} on the port-9490 session after 24 s of uptime, and {explorer:true, review:true} on the later port-9491 session whose cache held 'multi'. Parsing ~/Library/Application Support/Horus/last-workspace.json: 198,124 bytes, 3,026 paths, 12 statuses, root /Users/fuadnafiz98/Developer/materialx/materialsx-core-3, workspaceView 'file'. Also measured horus:snapshot-ready at 4,541.7 ms, i.e. beyond the 6 s budget once process spawn is added.
findings.fix: Stop probing DOM classes — the app already records exactly the milestones the benchmark wants. Replace scripts/benchmark-startup.mjs:102-108 with a probe that reads `performance.getEntriesByName('horus:explorer-committed')[0]?.startTime` and `performance.getEntriesByName('horus:viewer-committed')[0]?.startTime` (marked at RepositoryWorkspace.tsx:1297, MultiFileReview.tsx:1065 AND DiffSurface.tsx:535, so the viewer mark fires in both views), plus horus:react-committed and horus:snapshot-ready. That also removes the polling loop's 3 ms sampling error. If DOM probing is preferred, use `#repository-diff > *` (RepositoryWorkspace.tsx:887 sets id="repository-diff" on the diff panel). Raise HORUS_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS above the measured 4,541 ms snapshot-ready or the run will still time out on a real repo. Note separately that landing a dirty git repo in file view may itself be a product bug (App.tsx:907-909).
findings.estimatedGainMs: n/a — measurement correctness; without it no startup number can be trusted

findings.title: scripts/check-entry-chunk.mjs now guards a 2.8 KB Vite shim instead of the chunks that actually block mount
findings.mechanism: Since e18053e split main.tsx into a 9-line entry plus a boot chunk, the <script> in out/renderer/index.html points at index-CaNbrFQL.js, which is 2,816 bytes of Vite preload shim. The guard measures that against a 400 KB budget and greps it for 'WorkerPool'. Meanwhile boot-B2rRKoKF.js is 439,332 bytes — already over the budget the guard was written to enforce — and copyFilePath-C07D3-Xy.js, which does contain @pierre/diffs WorkerPoolManager (20,340 bytes of it), is a static dependency of WorkspaceRoot and therefore on the pre-mount path. The guard passes while the exact thing it was written to prevent has happened.
findings.evidence: out/renderer/index.html contains `<script type="module" crossorigin src="./assets/index-CaNbrFQL.js">`; that file is 2,816 bytes and is entirely the __vitePreload helper plus the shared sessionRestore/startupMetrics helpers. boot-B2rRKoKF.js is 439,332 bytes. copyFilePath-C07D3-Xy.js.map attributes 20,340 bytes to @pierre/diffs/dist/worker/WorkerPoolManager.js, and WorkspaceRoot-DzrbT5iL.js contains `from"./copyFilePath-C07D3-Xy.js"`.
findings.fix: Rewrite the script to walk the static import graph from the entry chunk plus the `boot` chunk and sum the transitive closure that boot.tsx preloads (WorkspaceRoot + its static deps + whichever viewer branch), then assert that total against a budget — start at the current ~1.9 MB and ratchet down as RB-01..RB-04 land. Keep the WorkerPool assertion but apply it to that closure, not to the shim. The graph can be parsed out of out/renderer/assets/*.js with the same `from"./X.js"` scan used in this audit, or emitted from a rollup manifest.
findings.estimatedGainMs: n/a — guardrail; its blind spot is what let 1.87 MB creep onto the pre-mount path unnoticed

findings.title: corner-shape: squircle is applied to the universal selector, putting every box on the superellipse paint path
findings.mechanism: The reset rule is `*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; corner-shape: squircle; }`. corner-shape replaces the rounded-rect corner geometry with a superellipse, a more expensive clip/paint path than the border-radius fast path, and it is declared on every element in the document — including the virtualized diff rows and the file-tree rows inside the two shadow roots. It only has a visible effect where border-radius is non-zero, which is a few dozen classes.
findings.evidence: styles.css:186-189 read directly. `grep -c 'corner-shape' src/renderer/src/styles.css` shows it also repeated inside the shadow-root CSS at RepositoryWorkspace.tsx:76-81. Live forced full style recalculation over the mounted tree is 0.20 ms, so the cost is not in matching — it would show in paint while scrolling, which I did not profile.
findings.fix: Move corner-shape out of the universal rule and onto the elements that actually round: `button, input, select, textarea, dialog, .card, .popover, kbd, [data-type="item"], .review-bar { corner-shape: squircle; }`. Keep box-sizing on `*`. Measure before/after with a paint profile while scrolling a large review, since the win is per-frame rather than at boot.
findings.estimatedGainMs: unmeasured at boot (full recalc is 0.2 ms); the plausible win is in scroll paint, not startup

findings.title: SidebarResizer forces a synchronous layout inside the first commit and can cause a second render
findings.mechanism: A useLayoutEffect reads `workspace.getBoundingClientRect().width` and then writes --sidebar-width on the same element. Reading geometry inside the first layout effect forces Chromium to lay out the freshly committed tree synchronously, inside the 91 ms boot long task. If clampSidebarWidth changes the value it also calls setCommittedWidth, producing a second render plus a localStorage write, and the effect re-runs because committedWidth is in its dependency array.
findings.evidence: SidebarResizer.tsx:28-41 read directly; the grep for synchronous layout reads across src/renderer/src found only three mount-time offenders and this is the only one on the boot path (RepositoryWorkspace.tsx:459-460 offsetWidth/offsetHeight is inside createTreeContextMenu, which only runs on right-click; MarkdownSplitResizer.tsx:80 and PerformanceChart.tsx:86 are interaction-time).
findings.fix: Set --sidebar-width from loadSidebarWidth() as an inline style on the .workspace element at render time (RepositoryWorkspace renders that parent) so no layout read is needed on the first pass, and clamp only from a ResizeObserver or window resize handler. That removes both the forced reflow and the possible second render.

findings.title: Explorer mount work is bounded and virtualized, but the tree reset does a per-directory collapse pass over every folder
findings.mechanism: Nothing renders 20,000 rows — @pierre/trees virtualizes correctly and there is no 20k-element React tree. What does scale with path count is the reset path: useFileTree is constructed with `paths: []` and then a layout effect calls model.resetPaths(treePaths) followed, for a git repo, by `for (const directoryPath of [...directoryPaths].reverse()) model.getItem(directoryPath)?.collapse()` — one model lookup and one collapse per directory, roughly 3,000-4,000 lookups on a 20k-path repo, on top of getDirectoryPaths itself.
findings.evidence: Live CDP probe: 218 light-DOM nodes, 1,291 including shadow roots, 2 shadow roots, 26 rendered tree rows. Bench (bun/JSC, V8 comparable): getDirectoryPaths 1.23 ms at 2,621 real paths / 11.06 ms at 20,000; new Set(paths) 0.82 ms at 20,000; createFileSearchIndex 0.46 ms / 3.18 ms. treeExpansion.ts:44-48 already documents that getDirectoryPaths was optimised from 133 ms to 25 ms at 40k paths, so this path has been tuned once already.
findings.fix: Pass the real paths to useFileTree at construction (it already accepts `paths` and `initialExpansion: 0`) so the model is built collapsed and the explicit collapse loop can be deleted for the initial mount, keeping it only for the incremental 'status' mode at RepositoryWorkspace.tsx:531-536. Independently, move createFileSearchIndex (useRepositorySearch.ts:42-45) behind requestIdleCallback so the fuzzy index is not built during the boot commit — the palette is already warmed on idle (App.tsx:977-982), so the index can be too.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 5-15 ms at mount on a large repo

findings.title: Confirmed clean — do not spend time here: StrictMode does not double-invoke in production, React Compiler is active, fonts do not block text paint
findings.mechanism: Three hypotheses worth ruling out, all negative. (1) StrictMode wraps the tree but the production react-dom build does not double-invoke, so it costs one extra component. (2) React Compiler genuinely runs — the problem is the App-specific bailout in RB-05, not the setup. (3) The two fontsource stylesheets are dynamically imported inside mountApp rather than statically at the entry, so they are off the pre-mount critical path and every face uses font-display: swap, meaning text paints immediately in the fallback.
findings.evidence: boot-B2rRKoKF.js.map attributes 176,999 bytes to react-dom/cjs/react-dom-client.production.js (no development build present). Memo-cache call counts in shipped chunks: boot 34, WorkspaceRoot 27, MultiFileReview 17; babel-plugin-react-compiler target 19 is wired at electron.vite.config.ts:216-220. Live `[...document.fonts]` reports 14 faces, every one `display=swap`, with only 'Inter Variable' latin and 'Fira Code Variable' latin in state 'loaded'; the built CSS confirms `font-display:swap` on every @font-face in opsz-DPutV6V0.css and wght-2hgtpDIl.css. first-contentful-paint at 284 ms coincides with React's commit, not with a font.
findings.fix: No change needed. One optional nit: the 133,336-byte inter-latin-ext woff2 is emitted and will be fetched the first time a non-ASCII character renders; drop the ext subsets from the fontsource import if that matters.

openQuestions: Why did React Compiler bail on App? The build has to be re-run with a logger on babel-plugin-react-compiler to get the reason. My best guesses from reading the source are the four useEffectEvent call sites (App.tsx:214, 758, 830, 894) or the mutable folderPickerOpenRef writes inside useCallback bodies (App.tsx:838-857), but I did not verify by rebuilding.

Was the blocking await in boot.tsx:20-30 added to suppress a visible skeleton flash? If so, does CachedWorkspaceFallback (App.tsx:326-357, capped at 120 rows) look bad enough to justify ~140 ms of blank window, or would a 60 ms delay before showing the fallback get both?

On restore, workspaceView is taken from the cache and App.tsx:907-909 never re-derives it because the cached paint already set appliedSnapshotRef to the same root. Is landing a dirty git repo in single-file view intended, or is that a product bug that also happens to break the startup benchmark (RB-09)?

I could not get a cold-start CPU profile: the app was already running and I deliberately did not restart the user's session. All timings here are warm — V8 code cache populated, asar pages in the OS page cache. A first-launch-after-update profile would likely show the 91 ms long task several times larger, which would raise RB-02 and RB-03 above RB-01 in priority.

Does @pierre/diffs actually execute shiki on the main thread, or is copyFilePath carrying it only for module-graph reasons? Three createHighlighter-family call sites are present in that chunk; whether any run at startup needs a breakpoint or CPU profile to settle before stubbing them (RB-03).

The 91 ms long task is one opaque block. Splitting it into module-eval vs React-render vs @pierre/trees model build needs Profiler.start + Page.reload over CDP, which requires restarting the app — worth doing once the user is not mid-session.

The lead's 1.9 MB / 20,000-path last-workspace.json is 10x the 198 KB / 3,026-path file I found on disk today. Which state is representative matters: at 20,000 paths RB-04/RB-05 (prepareFileTreeInput at 34.9 ms per App render) become the dominant renderer cost, whereas at 3,026 paths they are ~4 ms and RB-01 dominates.
